anomalies.obs: On the POWER TRAIN sheet the 'Reverse polarity protection' series element in the +24 V path is T3, an AON6407 (an N-channel MOSFET). Its gate (pin 2) is pulled up to the input rail through R7 (33 k) and clamped to GND by D3 (12 V zener), with source (pin 1) on the input side and drain (pin 3) on the output side. This is a P-channel drive topology: with source at +24 V the gate can only reach ~12 V, giving Vgs ≈ -12 V, which keeps an N-channel device permanently off.
anomalies.expected: A high-side reverse-polarity MOSFET switch driven this way must be a P-channel part (e.g. the SI2301 P-MOSFET that r1 used for this role). The spec's own component table even assigns AON6407 to a low-side application (the ATO-valve switch, where an N-channel is correct), not to this high-side position; the drawing instead put AON6407 in the series high-side slot and used A03400A (T5) for the valve.

evidence.quote: POWER TRAIN, sheet 1: 'Reverse polarity protection' over T3 AON6407 in the +24V series path; R7 33k from gate to +24V(in), D3 12V from gate to GND, source pin1 = input side, drain pin3 = +24V output.

"T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | Main circulation-pump ... ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch" and "r1's BOM lists ... T1 SI2301 P-MOSFET" (§5), i.e. the high-side reverse-polarity slot is a P-channel circuit.

anomalies.impact: The reverse-polarity protection MOSFET never enhances, so the 24 V rail is passed only through the body diode (≈0.7 V drop and extra dissipation) or, depending on the body-diode orientation as drawn, not at all. The intended low-loss MOSFET protection is defeated and the part is mis-applied for its position.

parsed.summary: Most of the drawing matches the specification (rails, isolators, TMC2209 sense resistors, pull-up values, DNP sensors, float interlocks), but the high-side 'reverse polarity protection' switch T3 is an N-channel AON6407 placed in a P-channel gate-drive topology (R7 pull-up to input, D3 zener to GND), so it cannot turn on as intended — a wrong-component-type anomaly.
